Characterised by extended convective envelopes, complex and dynamic atmospheres, and, sometimes, substantial mass loss, RSGs play a critical role in shaping both their own evolutionary outcomes and the circumstellar environments into which they ultimately explode. Despite decades of study, fundamental aspects of RSG physics remain poorly constrained, including the mechanisms driving mass loss and the connection between observed RSG populations and the properties of Type II supernovae. Recent observational advances have transformed the field, revealing episodic mass-loss events, asymmetric circumstellar structures, and signs of rapid evolutionary change in individual objects. Alongside these advances, studies of Type II supernovae and their progenitors have raised important new questions about the final stages of massive star evolution, including the possibility of rapid changes in the years immediately preceding core collapse. Motivated by these developments, this review aims to describe our current understanding of how RSGs live and die, from their observed properties through to their role as supernova progenitors, and where that understanding remains incomplete.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication. Invited review for the Universe special issue "The Lifecycle of Massive Stars" edited by Jacco van Loon

papers.t: 3D and 2D Radiation Non-ideal MHD modeling of the decay of FUor outbursts
papers.abs: FU Orionis (FUor) outbursts are high-accretion events in protoplanetary disks thought to be driven by the magnetorotational instability (MRI). Although these outbursts span a wide range of observed durations and can thermally process and potentially transport disk material, the physical processes governing their decay remain poorly understood. We present a three-dimensional radiative non-ideal magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulation of the decay of an MRI-driven FUor outburst, complemented by a suite of two-dimensional models that explore its dependence on disk properties. During the decay, rings and gaps form naturally within the inner disk. Magnetic flux preferentially concentrates in the gaps, while the rings remain comparatively weakly magnetized. We show that MRI-active rings act as ``magnetic dams,'' confining magnetic flux within adjacent gaps. As the rings cool below the MRI activation temperature, non-ideal MHD effects decouple the gas from the magnetic field, allowing the trapped flux to diffuse outward. This outward diffusion can sometimes transiently reactivate MRI in neighboring rings, producing localized reheating events that we term ``Reactivation.'' By comparing otherwise identical two- and three-dimensional simulations, we find that MRI heating is systematically less efficient in two dimensions, leading to outburst durations shorter by a factor of $\sim3$--4. Our model suite further shows that the decay timescale depends primarily on the disk surface density and distance from the central star, with only a weak dependence on the magnetic field strength. We further derive an empirical relation linking the outburst duration to these quantities.
papers.comment: 27 pages, 15 figures, accepted for publication in ApJ

papers.t: Exomoons and Exorings with the Habitable Worlds Observatory. III. Icy Moons and Rings Often Outshine Their Planets
papers.abs: If we could observe the Solar System's giant planets with the upcoming Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), the dominant sources of reflected near-infrared light would not always be the planets themselves. In fact, the brightest sources are split roughly evenly between the giants and their icy companions: at the locations of the giant planets, the dominant point sources would be Jupiter, Saturn's rings, Uranus, and Triton (Neptune's icy moon). Motivated by these Solar System cases in which rings or moons outshine their host planets, we investigate the detectability of analogous exomoons and exorings with HWO. We compute the expected signal-to-noise ratios (S/N) for moons and rings with the same albedos as their Solar System counterparts over a range of sizes, system distances, and star to planet+moon or star to planet+ring separations. We find that reflected light from Triton-analog exomoons and Saturn-analog exorings is detectable with HWO over a broad parameter space. In the nearest systems, icy Titan-sized moons are detectable at star-moon separations of ~2 AU and icy Earth-sized moons out to ~6 AU. Moreover, Saturn-like exorings are likely to be the brightest point sources in many extrasolar systems, capable of greatly outshining any planets, while remaining potentially detectable at system distances out to 100 pc. These results highlight the need for further work to develop methods for identifying and disentangling exoring and exomoon signatures from exoplanet signals in HWO observations, where these sources will be blended and spatially unresolved.

papers.t: Non-monotonic Age-metallicity Relations Across the Galactic Disk Revealed by APOGEE Red Clump Stars
papers.abs: Using APOGEE red clump stars and open clusters with precise ages, we investigate the age--metallicity relation (AMR) across the Galactic disk as a function of Galactocentric radius $R$ and vertical height $|Z|$. For stars older than $\sim$6--8 Gyr, the AMR shows little dependence on either $R$ or $|Z|$ within the uncertainties, suggesting rapid and well-mixed chemical evolution in the early disk. In contrast, younger populations exhibit a clear negative radial metallicity gradient, with the inner disk being more metal-rich than the outer disk, consistent with inside-out disk growth since $\sim$6--8 Gyr ago. Most importantly, at fixed location, the AMR for ages $\lesssim6$--8 Gyr is non-monotonic: [Fe/H] decreases toward younger ages, reaches a minimum at intermediate ages, and then rises again. Beyond $R\sim11$\,kpc, the relation becomes even more complex, exhibiting an additional reversal and a distinct metallicity peak at an age of $\sim2$\,Gyr. Such complex behavior cannot be explained by continuous local enrichment alone, but instead points to the combined effects of a multi-phase gas-accretion history and radial migration. Episodes of metal-poor gas inflow can dilute the interstellar medium and reset its chemical evolution, while subsequent enrichment raises the metallicity again; radial migration further reshapes the observed AMR by mixing stellar populations formed at different radii and metallicities. A toy model incorporating inside-out growth, two gas-inflow episodes, and radial migration qualitatively reproduces the observed trends, highlighting the combined roles of episodic gas accretion and radial migration in shaping the chemical evolution of the Galactic disk.
papers.comment: 15 pages, 6 figures, accepted for publication in ApJ

papers.t: On Modelling the Far-Side Unsigned Magnetic Flux Evolution of Long-Lived NOAA Active Regions
papers.abs: The evolution of magnetic flux in solar active regions is central to space-weather forecasting and solar-cycle studies. Direct measurements of the far-side magnetic field, however, remain unavailable with current solar instrumentation. We develop a method to estimate the far-side evolution of active-region magnetic flux using 304 Å (He II) emission as a quantitative proxy. Using SDO/AIA and SDO/HMI observations of all four near-side passages of a long-lived active region (NOAA AR 12192), we fit a single relation that gives mean per-pixel unsigned magnetic flux from mean per-pixel 304 Å intensity. The fit uses only disk-centre, flare-free intervals, and flux is the dependent variable, so the relation can be applied directly to intensity measurements. The magnetogram flux is deprojected to the radial direction before fitting, and we report the line-of-sight version for comparison. We first test the relation by fitting it on the first two passages and predicting the two later passages, which were not used in that fit; the relation adopted for the reconstruction is then fitted to all four passages. We then apply the same relation to STEREO-A/EUVI 304 Å observations, scaling the EUVI intensities to AIA-equivalent boundary intensities inferred from the adjacent near-side flux measurements, and so reconstruct the unsigned flux history while the region was out of view from Earth. The test on the later passages gives a median log-space residual of +0.052 dex, a root-mean-square error of 0.083 dex, and a median absolute fractional error of 14% over 272 samples that were not used in the fit. Because a single cross-instrument scale factor cannot match both ends of a far-side interval, the absolute level of each reconstructed segment carries an uncertainty of several tens of per cent; it is the shape of the far-side curve, rather than its level, that the EUVI observations constrain.
papers.comment: 15 pages, 8 figures, 5 tables. Accepted for publication in the Journal of Astrophysics and Astronomy (JAA)

papers.t: Current Accretion State versus Black Hole Mass: Imprints on Multiphase Gas in IllustrisTNG
papers.abs: The coupling between AGN feedback and the multiphase circumgalactic medium (CGM) is central to understanding galaxy evolution. In a previous paper, we showed that the black hole mass ($M_{\rm BH}$) correlates negatively with cold gas mass in IllustrisTNG100. We now extend this to the Eddington ratio ($λ_{\rm Edd}$), which traces the current accretion state, using the same sample of 5089 central galaxies at $z=0$ under the same group-specific partial correlation framework, controlling for stellar and dark matter halo mass. We find that $λ_{\rm Edd}$ correlates positively with warm gas in star-forming galaxies ($ρ\approx 0.6$-$0.7$), persisting after jointly controlling for $M_{\rm BH}$, the mass in the other non-star-forming gas phases, and specific star formation rate. The $λ_{\rm Edd}$-cold gas correlation instead reverses sign, from negative in star-forming galaxies ($ρ\approx -0.32$) to positive in quenched galaxies ($ρ\approx 0.40$). Controlling for $M_{\rm BH}$ leaves this correlation essentially unchanged in all three galaxy types. Further controlling for the total gas mass in the other phases strengthens the star-forming correlation and weakens the quenched correlation to $ρ\approx 0.21$, which remains significant. These results establish the Eddington ratio as a phase- and type-dependent tracer of the gas-black hole connection: the cold gas reservoir records the integrated black hole growth, the warm gas in star-forming galaxies carries the signature of the current accretion state, and the sign reversal of the cold-gas correlation marks the transition between the star-forming and quenched regimes.

papers.t: Depolarization of Synchrotron Polarization in Magnetized Interstellar Media
papers.abs: We numerically study three key depolarization mechanisms of synchrotron polarization, including wavelength independent depolarization, differential Faraday rotation depolarization, and beam depolarization, across subAlfvénic and superAlfvénic turbulent regimes. Using 3D MHD simulations and synthetic observations, we analyze their effects on polarization degree and power spectra. We find that (1) SubAlfvénic turbulence shows high but strongly suppressed polarization under Faraday rotation, while superAlfvénic turbulence remains low and stable; (2) Differential Faraday depolarization dominates in ordered subAlfvénic media. For disordered superAlfvénic regimes, beam depolarization dominates at high frequencies, while at low frequencies it saturates and differential Faraday depolarization takes over as the dominant mechanism; and (3) Depolarization significantly distorts spectra in superAlfvénic turbulence but weakly affects subAlfvénic cases. Our results provide a quantitative basis for correcting depolarization biases in magnetic turbulence measurements with radio polarization data.
papers.comment: 18 pages, 10 figures, 1 table, accepted for publication in ApJ

papers.t: Integrating AI Coding Agents Into Scientific Research
papers.abs: New software tools have emerged that enable AI agents to quickly develop code that analyzes data and generates figures, but their mistakes can also harm a researcher's computer, require extensive resources for validation, and cause the results to be received more skeptically. These concerns could be mitigated if scientific software is developed in a secure environment with a system for monitoring file changes and well-defined standards for handling AI agents. This paper first describes how coding agents change eleven aspects of generating, verifying, and reproducing numerical results. A six-level scale is then proposed for classifying AI-assisted numerical experiments by their provenance, reproducibility, openness, oversight, and falsifiability (PROOF). The scale begins with locally self-consistent, version-controlled, human-verified results and culminates in a publicly accessible and curated archive of the files, change history, prompt transcripts, independent agent regeneration of the analysis, and multiple cryptographically verifiable attestations of regeneration by independent researchers. These aspects of AI-assisted scientific software development have been synthesized into a new open source software package called vaibify that optimizes the agentic development of computational experiments ascending the PROOF Ladder. Docker containers sequester the agents while a GUI enables researchers to prompt command line agents, monitor the current status of local and remote files, and drive a project to PROOF Level 3 (reproducible). The methods described in this paper could help researchers reduce the time required to verify agent-written software and efficiently communicate trust in AI-assisted science.
papers.comment: 36 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables. Software publicly available at https://github.com/RoryBarnes/vaibify

papers.t: Theoretical Instability Models of Quasi-Periodic Eruptions
papers.abs: The nature of the Quasi-Periodic Eruptions (QPE) is still not firmly established while the phenomenon probes the innermost part of the accretion flow undergoing dramatic changes. In this chapter we review the possibility that the observed rapid variability is caused by the accretion disk instability. We summarise the defining observational properties of QPE sources: time scales of recurrence, the amplitudes of soft X-ray flares, high coherence over many cycles, and comparatively modest time-averaged luminosities. We then translate these into constraints on the characteristic radius, accretion rate, and energy reservoir of the inner disk. We review the main classes of disk instabilities relevant to supermassive black holes: radiation pressure induced thermal/viscous limit cycles, magnetically mediated inner disk transitions, and coupling to disk winds that can produce the oscillatory behavior. For each scenario we discuss the required parameter space (black hole mass, Eddington ratio, viscosity prescription, and truncation radius), the predicted spectral and timing signatures, and the degree of fine tuning needed to reproduce the observed duty cycles and flare morphologies. We highlight key tensions, including the extremely soft spectra, short recurrence times compared with standard viscous times at tens of gravitational radii, and the weak or absent contemporaneous optical/UV variability in several systems. Finally, we outline observational tests that may help distinguish between instability driven and geometrical or orbital models: phase resolved spectroscopy to track the temperature evolution, searches for hysteresis in hardness-intensity diagrams, reverberation and absorption variability tied to winds, and long baseline monitoring to measure drift in period and energy output.
papers.comment: 25 pages; Invited review chapter for the book "Mysterious Repeating Signals from Centers of Galaxies" (Eds. Dheeraj Pasham, Eric Coughlin, Riccardo Arcodia, Petra Sukova, Itai Linial, Springer Singapore, expected in 2027). After first referee report, comments welcome

papers.t: The interplay between ionized and warm molecular gas in the turbulent intragroup medium of Stephan's Quintet
papers.abs: Using JWST MIRI spectroscopy, we explore the multi-phase intergalactic gas in the hot halo of the Stephan's Quintet compact group. Unlike the coolest H2 emission, which commonly shows double- peaked profiles corresponding to the velocity of the intruder and the intragroup gas, the ionized Neon emission-lines are often systematically shifted redwards in radial velocity away from the lowest H2 peak, and into the region corresponding to gas decelerated by the collision of the intruder galaxy with intragroup gas. The majority of the brightest clumps of ionized gas are spatially correlated with the brightest H2 clumps, suggesting they are coherent structures caught up in the opposing gas flows. Gas that is progressively heated, is shifted in velocity further from the velocity of the coldest H2 peaks. Larger and larger shifts in velocity are seen as one progresses from cool to warm molecular hydrogen, to lower-excitation (Neon lines) ionized and strongly shocked heated ionized gas (gas-phase Iron). The majority of the ionized Neon in the intergalactic medium is consistent with excitation in low-velocity shocks. We suggest that this behavior is the result of gas of progressively lower densities being shocked and accelerated by the interaction of pre-existing clouds with a hot flow created by the blast-wave from the collision between the intruder and the intragroup gas. One exception is the extragalactic star forming region, SQ-A, which shows higher-excitation ionized emission lines consistent with heating from a young starburst, consistent with previous photometry of young star clusters in the region.
papers.comment: 21 pages, 7 figures: Accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal, November 2026

papers.t: VLA Observations of the Ionized Jet IRAS 16562-3959
papers.abs: We present new high-resolution, high-sensitivity Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA) A-configuration observations of the high-mass protostellar jet system IRAS 16562-3959 at 3.1 and 6.1 GHz. Our images resolve the five previously known jet components (OE, IE, C, IW, OW) into 21 distinct knots and sub-components, and reveal a new off-axis source, MW. Based on the dynamical timescales from previous works ($τ_{jet} \approx 620$ yr), the spacing and structure of the knots suggest episodic accretion with a mean interval between ejections of $\sim$32 yr. We find that source MW has a substantial increase in peak brightness relative to its marginal detections in previous observations. MW exhibits a spectral index of $α\approx -0.7$, characteristic of synchrotron emission from shock-accelerated relativistic electrons. Equipartition analysis yields a minimum-energy magnetic field strength $B_{me} \approx 0.4$ mG, and a minimum total energy $E_{me} \approx 4.4 \times 10^{42}$ erg. Archival 2MASS Ks data imply a total outflow dynamical age of $\sim$1400 yr, and together with a HST [FeII] 1.64 $μ$m map, the NIR data indicate that the fast jet is embedded in a wide-angle wind with a $\sim 36^\circ$ opening angle.
papers.comment: 18 pages, 8 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal on Nov 10, 2026

papers.t: Fundamental physics with quantum sensors in space
papers.abs: Quantum sensors such as atomic clocks, atom interferometers, and atomic magnetometers can be used as sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model. Space offers microgravity, long baselines, low environmental noise, access to varying gravitational potentials, and unique opportunities involving the Sun, Moon, planets, and asteroids. These proceedings of the Aspen Center for Physics workshop on "Fundamental physics in space with quantum sensors," held February 22-27, 2026, summarize the scientific case, current capabilities, and space mission concepts for investigating dark matter, testing general relativity, and detecting gravitational waves in frequency bands inaccessible from the ground.

papers.t: Unveiling the infrared excess of SIPS J2045-6332 II: SPHEREx spectral decomposition supports a young unresolved binary interpretation
papers.abs: SIPS J2045-6332 is an unusual low-mass object previously identified by its infrared excess and possible signatures of youth and unresolved multiplicity. Earlier work suggested that it is relatively young and may host a mid-L companion. Here we reassess the system using low-resolution 0.75-5 micron spectroscopy from SPHEREx. We perform single- and binary-template spectral decomposition with field-gravity and intermediate-gravity (beta) templates spanning M8-L4. Binary-template models consistently outperform single-template models, most strongly for the beta templates. The preferred solution, an L0beta + L1beta combination (reduced chi^2 = 10.72), best matches the combined-light spectrum, although M9beta + L1beta and M9beta + L2beta give comparably good fits. Combining bolometric luminosities from gravity-dependent bolometric corrections (log L/Lsun = -3.42 +/- 0.08 and -3.85 +/- 0.09) with the Sonora evolutionary models, we estimate component masses of ~0.015 and ~0.011 Msun at 25 Myr and >~0.043-0.046 and ~0.038-0.043 Msun at 200-250 Myr for the primary and secondary (primary values are lower limits), implying a mass ratio q <~ 0.7-0.9, i.e. a companion of comparable but not necessarily equal mass. These results independently reinforce previous interpretations that SIPS J2045-6332 is a relatively young unresolved binary, and demonstrate the capability of SPHEREx spectroscopy to characterise young low-mass binaries through spectral decomposition.

papers.t: A Catalog of Young Stellar Objects in the Lagoon Nebula
papers.abs: M8, the Lagoon Nebula, has been known for more than 100 years as a region forming stars. It is (in projection) very close to if not in the Galactic Bulge. As a result, the source surface density is very high and source confusion is a substantial challenge. Because of the location, there have been many surveys that serendipitously observed M8, in addition to studies specifically targeting it. But to this point, there has been no effort to resolve source confusion across all the existing catalogs, spanning many different wavelengths, sensitivities, and spatial resolutions. We have done all of this source reconciliation, and present the merged catalog here. The net result is 3019 YSOs with largely photometric data and/or YSO selection from ~50 different origins, primarily ranging from $g$-band through 25 um, but with a significant number of X-ray sources, and some data of limited sensitivity out through 70-450 um. The catalog includes several flags that enable users to select, e.g., the YSOs that have been identified as young by the most studies, or the YSOs with the most multi-wavelength counterparts, or the ones with the clearest IR excesses. We use this catalog in a companion paper; it will also be of use in, e.g., future SPHEREx and Roman work.
papers.comment: Accepted by ApJS; figures degraded in resolution for arXiv

papers.t: Euclid DR1 Legacy Science on Ultracool Dwarfs: Halpha activity, kinematic age and rotation of M7--L1 dwarfs from DESI DR1, SPHEREx and Euclid
papers.abs: The fraction of late-M dwarfs with detectable Halpha rises toward the stellar-substellar boundary while their emission weakens relative to the bolometric luminosity, a contrast attributed to the fading continuum. We measure how much of this rise the continuum explains and whether younger populations or longer activity lifetimes contribute. We select 8939 dwarfs of type M7 or later, all but 22 of them M7-L1, from DESI DR1. We compare active fractions at common thresholds in equivalent width and in log(L_Ha/L_bol), the Halpha-to-bolometric luminosity ratio, in spectra sensitive to each threshold. We jointly model continuum fading, emission weakening and an extra active component. Kinematics use Gaia astrometry and DESI radial velocities for dwarfs with G = 5) test the optical type scale, and VIS images resolve three close binaries (0.22-0.53 arcsec) with common proper motion. We confirm that the rise in equivalent-width incidence comes mostly from the fading continuum acting on weakening emission. Conditional on an age-velocity relation and uniform ages, a step model gives thin-disk activity lifetimes at log(L_Ha/L_bol) = -4.7 of 5.9 (5.3-6.6) and 6.4 (5.2-8.0) Gyr at M7 and M8. Both bins contain mostly stars, so these lifetimes describe the lowest-mass stars.

papers.t: Rapid Protoplanetary Disk Evolution and Debris Disk Formation in Taurus-Auriga
papers.abs: We present a Submillimeter Array (SMA) 1.3mm (225GHz) continuum emission survey of Young Stellar Objects (YSOs) in the Taurus-Auriga star-forming region, comprising 69 class III and 5 class I/II YSOs with spectral types B9-M3, as part of a total sample of 149 class II and 82 class III YSOs. This represents a complete sample (100%) of class II and III YSOs with spectral types earlier than K3, and a near-complete sample (85%) for spectral types earlier than M2. The survey has a median $3σ$ sensitivity of 1.4mJy. We did not find any emission from circumstellar dust around class III YSOs, but present three detections that can be attributed to variable stellar activity, and one from an unresolved companion. We compile and model spectral energy distributions (SEDs) for the sample, and report 27 class III YSOs with excess thermal emission. We demonstrate that the class III YSOs in Taurus are typically older than their class II counterparts. We produce millimeter luminosity and dust disk mass distributions, and present evidence for a bifurcation between the class II and III populations, implying that ${\gtrsim}99.5\%$ of the dust mass is dispersed or transformed as YSOs transition from the class II to III stage. The combined infrared and millimeter properties demonstrate that warm (inner) and cold (outer) dust reservoirs evolve on comparable timescales: there is a rapid evolution across the radial extent of disks. We demonstrate that the survey properties are broadly consistent with a belt population that formed planetesimals from class II disks with an efficiency of a few tenths to a few tens of percent.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ. 28 pages (inc. tables, appendices, 10 figures)

papers.t: A search for optical bursts from the repeating fast radio burst in the M81 globular cluster, FRB 20200120E
papers.abs: We present a search for optical bursts from the repeating fast radio burst FRB 20200120E, which is located in a globular cluster of M81 and is the closest known extragalactic FRB. We observed FRB 20200120E simultaneously with the high-speed, quintuple-beam optical camera HiPERCAM on the 10.4-m Gran Telescopio Canarias and the Effelsberg 100-m Radio Telescope. We detected one radio burst of fluence $\mathcal{F}_{\rm R} = 0.14\pm0.01$ Jy ms during our observations, but found no evidence for corresponding optical bursts in the 11.98 ms frames. We find 5$σ$ upper limits on the optical burst fluence of $\mathcal{F}_{\rm O} < 1.8\times10^{-3}$ Jy ms (combined $u_s g_s r_s i_s z_s$-bands) and the optical burst energy of $E_{\rm O} < 5.4\times10^{36}$ erg ($r_s$-band), corrected for interstellar extinction. We compare our upper limit on the optical-to-radio fluence ratio $\mathcal{F}_{\rm O}/\mathcal{F}_{\rm R} < 0.013$ to various emission models involving inverse-Compton scattering in the magnetosphere or nebula of a highly-magnetised neutron~star.
papers.comment: 7 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables, accepted for publication in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

papers.t: Improved accuracy of the reference photon calibration standards in the network of gravitational-wave observatories during the O4 observing run
papers.abs: The global network of gravitational wave observatories uses systems known as Photon Calibrators to provide absolute calibration via laser radiation pressure. Successive detector improvements are increasing sensitivity, enabling not only increase the detection rate but also detections with high signal to noise ratios. To optimally extract information from these detected signals, continual effort is directed at pushing the state of the art of the interferometer calibration accuracy. To improve the accuracy of the locally-maintained laser power standards for photon calibration, a new global calibration scheme was implemented by using transfer standards calibrated at both the National Institute of Standards and Tech- nology (NIST) in the US and the Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB) in Germany during the recently completed fourth observing run. We report the results of a long-duration NIST-PTB bilateral comparison conducted over almost three years and the results of propagation of transfer standard calibrations to the reference power sensors maintained at each observatory.

papers.t: Three Dimensional Structure of Jovian Polar Cyclones Revealed by Juno Microwave Radiometer
papers.abs: Jupiter's circumpolar cyclones (CPCs) represent one of the most extreme dynamical regimes of the Solar System, where rotation, stratification, and convection interact to organize a stable polygonal cyclone lattice at each pole. Yet the depth and vertical structure of these cyclones remain unresolved. Here, using Juno Microwave Radiometer observations acquired between May 2023 and May 2024, we retrieve the 3-D thermal/compositional structure of Jupiter's northern CPCs at depths beyond those detectable by Earth-based telescopes and spacecraft that have ever visited. The eight CPCs, appearing with enhanced microwave brightness, show as modest ammonia depletion near the water lifting-condensation level ($\sim$5 bar) and/or, equivalently, warm-core structures analogous to terrestrial tropical cyclones. Five of them show substantially stronger and deeper anomalies than the remaining three, with approximately twice the inferred ammonia depletion and localized heating. In contrast, the central polar cyclone exhibits little microwave brightness contrast relative to its surroundings, despite its substantially cloudier and visually distinct appearance in visible and infrared observations. Previous dynamical models have treated the CPCs and the central polar cyclone as dynamically similar structures arising from the self-organization of turbulent flows. The new observations, however, suggest that the CPCs and the central polar cyclone may have distinct origins and operate under different dynamical regimes.

papers.t: Super-Eddington Accretion onto Compact Objects: Theory Meets Observation
papers.abs: We review candidate super-Eddington populations together with semi-analytic models and radiation magnetohydrodynamic simulations, with the following conclusions: $\bullet$ Likely super-Eddington sources over a range of black hole mass show similar properties, including outflow on a range of scales, hard X-ray weakness, decreased emission from jets, and suppressed optical/UV variability. $\bullet$ Theoretical treatment of super-Eddington accretion predicts similar behavior across a range of methods and initial conditions, although interesting differences remain, particularly in the importance of magnetic fields. Numerical simulations produce a puffed-up inner disk with a funnel that grows narrower at higher mass accretion rate. Radiative efficiency declines with accretion rate in thermal-pressure--supported disks. $\bullet$ Ubiquitous outflow is likely an important ingredient in galaxy feedback at high Eddington ratios, as wind mechanical power increases with accretion rate and can rival jet power. Wind kinetic power depends far less on uncertain black hole spin and magnetic fields. $\bullet$ Observational classes of objects can be sorted in a two-dimensional parameter space of Eddington ratio and orientation. Observations down the funnel observe rapid X-ray variability, while observations through the wind will see suppressed X-ray emission. At the highest Eddington ratios, we envision a regime where the photosphere extends to $r > 10^6 \, r_g$, and the observer sees only thermalized emission covering most of the sky, speculatively corresponding to super-soft sources and Little Red Dots.
papers.comment: 49 pages, 6 figures, author-approved manuscript version, to be published in ARA&A

papers.t: D/H and 12C/13C ratios of benzonitrile and indene in TMC-1 support bottom-up formation of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon-like molecules
papers.abs: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) have recently been detected in cold dark clouds through their rotational spectra, but it is currently a matter of debate whether they form through a bottom-up process from small hydrocarbons or through a top-down scenario involving the fragmentation of large PAHs inherited from a previous evolutionary stage of diffuse cloud. Isotopic ratios can shed light on the origin of PAHs in cold dark clouds. Large aromatic molecules observed in the infrared are enriched in deuterium and may also be enriched in 13C because they likely formed in the ejecta of evolved stars. We synthesized indene deuterated at the aliphatic position in the laboratory and measured its rotational spectrum, together with those of the nine 13C singly substituted isotopomers of indene. We used the measured spectra of the D and 13C isotopic species of indene, together with previously measured spectra of D and 13C isotopic benzonitrile, to search for these species in the cold dark cloud TMC-1 using QUIJOTE data obtained with the Yebes 40m telescope. We used a line stack method to tentatively detect deuterated benzonitrile and detect 13C-substituted benzonitrile, but find no evidence of either the D or 13C isotopic species of indene. We derive an aromatic D/H ratio of 0.53 % from benzonitrile, an aliphatic D/H ratio 55 for benzonitrile and indene, respectively. These values are consistent with isotopic ratios derived for other molecules in TMC-1 and show no enrichment in either D or 13C that could be ascribed to inheritance from large PAHs in a top-down scenario; a bottom-up scenario is therefore the most likely.

papers.t: A Forecast for Testing the Decreasing H₀ Trend in Time-Delay Cosmography
papers.abs: In 2019 the H0LiCOW/TDCOSMO collaboration reported a decreasing Hubble constant $H_0$ trend with lens redshift in the flat $Λ$CDM model at low statistical significance ($< 2 σ$). The signal is expected if physics is missing from the $Λ$CDM model in the late universe. In the wake of recent TDCOSMO 2026 results, we revisit the feature. Although the statistical significance of the trend has increased in a like-for-like comparison with earlier studies, propagating mass-sheet transformation (MST) uncertainties reduces the significance to $\sim 1 σ$. As a result, Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) currently favours a constant $H_0$ over a decreasing $H_0$ in the ratio 2.4:1. Nevertheless, we highlight good agreement on a negative slope with independent observables and forecast that approximately 40 and 90 lenses will be required to substantiate the trend at $\sim 2 σ$ and $\sim 3 σ$ significance, respectively, if the feature is physical and current uncertainties are representative. Even now, it is evident that the TDCOSMO 2026 $H_0$ constraint $H_0 \approx 71$ km/s/Mpc reflects an average over the lens redshift distribution and is naturally anchored at intermediate lens redshifts.

papers.t: Comparative analysis of two delta Scuti stars approaching the TAMS using MESA-GYRE models
papers.abs: This study presents a comparative asteroseismic analysis of two late main-sequence \dss\ with slow to moderate rotation, TIC 274211446 and TIC 16053262. Both are also characterised by showing an intense emission in the H$_α$ line. Based on the first 35 extracted frequencies from short-cadence photometric data from the TESS mission, with no significant pulsations out of the [9, 40] \cd range, I estimated the large frequency separation. I calibrated evolutionary and adiabatic oscillation models using the \mesa\ and \gyre\ codes under the Traditional Approximation of Rotation (TAR). I used the observed large separation and spectroscopic temperature to constrain the models. Finally, I have used kernel curve fitting (KDE) to find the best profiles for both stars. With a hydrogen fraction of 21$\%$ in the convective core, TIC~274211446 is more evolved than TIC~16053262, which still retains 30$\%$ of its core fuel. The former has a large separation $Δν$ = (2.7$\pm$0.1) \cd, and points to a model with M = (1.84$\pm$0.07) M$_{\odot}$, a radius of R = (2.67$\pm$0.07) R$_{\odot}$, and an effective temperature of \teff = (7308$\pm$71) K. The latter, with $Δν$ = (3.25$\pm$0.1) \cd, points to a more compact model with M = (1.72$\pm$0.07)M$_{\odot}$, R = (2.28$\pm$0.05)R$_{\odot}$, and \teff = (7298$\pm$59) K. The equatorial rotation velocities are (28$\pm$1) \kms\ and (47$\pm$13) \kms, respectively. TIC~274211446 has an age of (1070$\pm$127) \myr, and TIC~16053262 is (1145$\pm$165) \myr\ old.

papers.t: Brown dwarfs and stars are dynamically indistinguishable as companions in AU-separation binaries
papers.abs: Brown dwarfs occupy the mass range between stars and planets, populations whose dominant formation channels differ, which leave measurable differences in the orbital eccentricity and host-star metallicity distributions. We assemble a sample of astrometric binaries with main sequence primaries and brown dwarf companions at $\mathcal{O}$(AU) separations from $\textit{Gaia}$ DR3. The observable photocenter motions for such binaries are degenerate between a genuinely low-mass companion and a near-equal-mass binary. We break this degeneracy using $\textit{Gaia}$ XP spectrophotometry and follow-up FEROS spectroscopy, which removes removes ${\sim}70\%$ of initial low-mass-function candidates as likely near-twin binaries and leaves residual contamination of only a few percent. The resulting 368 systems, with masses and metallicities determined from the XP spectra and a selection function forward-modelled with $\texttt{Gaiamock}$, form the largest homogeneous sample of brown dwarf companions with astrometric orbits. We find the eccentricity distribution to be well described by a normal distribution. This is comparable to eccentricities of stellar companions at the same periods and higher than those of giant planets, with no significant dependence on companion mass ($α=-0.13\pm0.09$) or period ($β=0.10\pm0.05$). The host-star metallicity distribution is likewise stellar-like, extending to [M/H]$=-0.5$, in contrast to the predominantly super-solar metallicity hosts of giant planets. After accounting for selection, the companion-mass distribution over all brown dwarf masses is consistent with an extension of stellar-binary demographics. Brown dwarf companions at AU separations down to at least $20\,M_J$ therefore appear to form predominantly through a binary-star-like channel. A possible transition to planet-like formation at lower masses cannot be located with the present sample.
papers.comment: Submitted to A&A November 16th, 2026. Comments welcome

papers.t: Spectro-Spatial Survey Fusion
papers.abs: Imaging and spectroscopy constrain complementary information about the same sky but are usually processed separately. We introduce Spectro-Spatial Survey Fusion, a framework that unifies these measurements by fitting a continuous spectral surface-brightness field jointly through each instrument's response. Adapting from Gaussian splatting in computer vision, we represent the field as a sum of adaptive spatial Gaussians, each carrying a spectrum built from a shared, learned dictionary of templates. We demonstrate this on 400 Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) $ugriz$ exposures and 800 fiber spectra across an $84^{\prime}\times84^{\prime}$ region of COSMOS. The joint fit closely reproduces the spatial structure and broad spectral diversity of galaxies, stars, and quasars. For fitted SDSS observations, the summed predicted flux in source-selected pixels agrees with the data to within 2 percent in every band, and 96 percent of fitted spectra agree to within 10 percent in integrated flux. Sparse fiber spectra constrain a dictionary shared by every Gaussian component, so a model spectrum can be queried anywhere in the imaged area, including where no spectrum was fitted. Without refitting, the field predicts withheld SDSS images and spectra, and selected Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC) images and Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectra, which never enter the fit. The field predicts broad spiral-arm patterns in HSC images of two selected galaxies and DESI continuum shapes for galaxies without a fitted fiber. This framework provides a route to combining surveys so that spatial and spectral information from different observations and instruments can constrain a common representation of the sky.

papers.t: A Single-Shot Method for the Absolute Polarization Angle Calibration of CMB Telescopes with Artificial Sky Sources via Stellar Diffraction Encoding
papers.abs: Absolute polarization angle calibration of cosmic microwave background (CMB) telescopes at the $\lesssim 0.1^\circ$ level is needed to prevent instrumental mixing of $E$ modes into $B$ modes from biasing constraints on primordial gravitational waves and cosmic birefringence. Artificial polarized sky sources like drones, balloons, or satellites can provide calibration references, but transferring their emitted polarization angle from the payload frame to the celestial frame remains a challenge. We propose a calibrator architecture, applicable to any such source, in which a single dual-use grid-optic sets the polarization axis of the emitted millimeter-wave signal and also diffracts starlight into a co-aligned star camera. The resulting diffraction spectra record the grid's orientation relative to the stars, so that it can be measured directly on the sky without fine alignment between the camera and grid-optic. We describe the geometry and physics of this concept and show that it significantly simplifies obtaining the calibration angle the observatory needs, because precise payload attitude is no longer needed and the received polarization is insensitive to small line-of-sight errors. In simulations of 1000 real star fields that include camera-grid misalignment, lens distortion, lateral chromatic aberration, atmospheric refraction, and stellar colors, a single exposure recovers the polarizing grid-optic's orientation in the celestial frame with an uncertainty of $\simeq 0.002^\circ$, fifty times below the $0.1^\circ$ goal. We also discuss the hardware tolerances a physical calibrator must meet, which future work will test. Our results establish the feasibility of this approach and motivate development of a dual-use grid-optic.

papers.t: A 15-year K-band view of long-period variables in the central region of M33
papers.abs: Long-period variables (LPVs) on the asymptotic giant branch (AGB) trace the late stages of stellar evolution and the return of mass to the interstellar medium. Their periods range from about 100 to 2000 d, so a few-year near-infrared campaign covers too few cycles for the slowest pulsators. We combine four independent UKIRT $K$-band data sets obtained between 2003 and 2018 into a homogeneous catalogue of the central $\approx$12 arcmin$^2$ of M33: 847 stars with 21085 measurements over 15.11 yr. Using 82 calibration stars, we place all data on the 2MASS/Vega system and remove inter-dataset offsets of up to 0.22 mag. Of the 847 stars, 771 are variable ($σ_K>0.10$ mag), and 385 have peak-to-peak amplitudes $A_K\geq1.0$ mag, which makes them Mira candidates. Of the 156 stars with Spitzer/IRAC [3.6] photometry, 120 have $\langle K\rangle-[3.6]>0.5$ mag and are candidate dust-enshrouded AGB stars. The catalogue is the basis for a forthcoming period-luminosity and star-formation history analysis
papers.comment: Proceedings of the BAO Conference 2026, submitted to Communications of the Byurakan Astrophysical

papers.t: Long-Term Spectral and Timing Variability of PKS 2155-304 from {\it Chandra} and {\it NuSTAR} Observations
papers.abs: Blazars exhibit strong variability across the electromagnetic spectrum, on timescales from minutes to decades. We present a study of the spectral and timing variability of the TeV blazar PKS~2155$-$304 using {\it Chandra} and {\it NuSTAR} observations spanning 25 years (1999$-$2024). Timing analysis reveals fractional variability amplitudes of up to $F_{\rm var}\approx 24\%$ in the hard X-ray band and $F_{\rm var}\lesssim 7.5\%$ in the soft X-ray band, along with variable power-spectral indices across observations. The minimum variability timescale, $τ_{\rm var} = 1.15\pm0.26$~ks, limits the size of the X-ray emitting region to $R \lesssim 7.7 \times 10^{14}$~cm, consistent with synchrotron emission from a compact region in the jet. We fitted the spectra using power-law (PL), broken power-law (BPL), log-parabola (LP), and bremsstrahlung plus power-law (BR+PL) models, the latter used only as a phenomenological description of the spectral curvature. The BPL model provides the best statistical description for most {\it Chandra} spectra. An F-test confirms a curved model over PL for all {\it Chandra} spectra, whereas most {\it NuSTAR} spectra are consistent with a single PL. Hardness ratio analysis shows a harder-when-brighter trend in the {\it Chandra} band. Joint fitting of the simultaneous 2013 {\it Chandra} and {\it NuSTAR} observations shows that the broadband 0.4$-$79~keV curvature is confined to the soft X-ray band, with the spectrum steepening above $\sim$2~keV and a steep hard X-ray power law ($Γ\simeq 2.7$). Our results reveal energy-dependent X-ray variability over more than two decades, and show that broadband X-ray coverage is needed to locate the curvature of the synchrotron tail in high-synchrotron-peaked blazars.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ. 25 pages, 13 figures and 6 tables

papers.t: Neutron-Rich Disks, Nickel-Rich Ejecta: Can Direct-Horizon Collapsars Explain Early r-Process Enrichment?
papers.abs: Very massive stars above the pair-instability mass gap may collapse directly into black holes surrounded by massive disks. These "direct-horizon collapsars" accrete at $\dot{M} \gtrsim 10\,M_\odot\,{\rm s}^{-1}$ and have been proposed to eject a substantial amount of $r$-process material, powering "super-kilonovae". We present the first three-dimensional general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations of direct-horizon collapsars with M1 neutrino transport, following a $\approx 150\,M_\odot$ helium core from collapse through the escape of magnetically driven outflows. Extreme accretion rates neutronize the disks to $Y_{\rm e} \approx 0.1$-$0.25$ and, at early times, allow them to satisfy the gravitational-instability and cooling criteria for fragmentation. However, the strong poloidal fields needed to eject the neutron-rich gas promptly also drain the disks and lift their electron degeneracy. The neutron-rich ejecta composition is set in a brief phase, such that the ejecta carry $\sim 0.1$-$0.3\,M_\odot$ of nuclei with $A \geq 69$, including $\lesssim 2\times10^{-4}\,M_\odot$ of lanthanides, alongside $\sim 1$-$4\,M_\odot$ of $^{56}$Ni. Assuming proportional retention and mixing of Eu and Fe, these yields imply $[{\rm Eu/Fe}]\approx-0.4$ to $+0.3$, and simple dilution estimates permit enrichment at $[{\rm Fe/H}]\lesssim-2.6$. Direct-horizon collapsars are therefore potential prompt contributors to iron and $r$-process enrichment at low metallicity. Their predicted Eu/Fe ratios fall below those of strongly $r$-process-enhanced stars, but uncertainties in the relative yields, particularly of iron, may close this gap. The ${}^{56}{\rm Ni}$-rich ejecta would power luminous supernovae with rise times of weeks, potentially accompanied by exceptionally powerful gamma-ray bursts, rather than lanthanide-rich super-kilonovae.
papers.comment: 23 pages, 10 figures (5 in appendix). Comments welcome. Submitted for publication

papers.t: Connecting Calcium Depletion and Dust Evolution in the Rapid Accretor T28
papers.abs: We present a multi-wavelength case study of the star T28 in the Chamaeleon I star-forming region and investigate the dust evolution of its highly Ca-depleted protoplanetary disk. We combine new observations from the MIKE spectrograph on the Magellan Clay Telescope with archival IRS spectrum and photometry. We constrain the optical extinction using the hydrogen column density of the region, and apply ROTFIT to obtain stellar parameters. We estimate the mass accretion rate by fitting the excess flux above the photosphere with an accretion shock model. We model the line profiles of Ca II K and H$α$ with magnetospheric accretion models to infer Ca/H abundance, while the infrared excess is modeled with irradiated accretion disk models to get disk properties. We find that T28 is a high accretor with significant Ca depletion in its accretion flows. We find that the disk is best fit with a pre-transitional model with a disk mass of 0.12 $M_{\odot}$, where two optically thick disks are separated by a gap filled with optically thin dust extending to 16 au. This gap would not be resolved in the existing observations. T28 follows the trend of increasing depletion with increasing mass accretion rate. This trend can potentially be explained by preferential and early giant planet formation in massive disks, as suggested by recent planet formation simulations, leading to enhanced capture of refractory material in the massive disks of high accretors and thus depletion in the material reaching the star.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal

papers.t: Cross-correlating the SPHEREx extragalactic background light with CMB lensing II: theoretical predictions confronted with lightcone simulations
papers.abs: Cross-correlating intensity maps with the lensing of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) rejects the foregrounds and noise that do not trace the dark matter. In the near infrared, the remaining signal combines the integrated galaxy light (IGL), the intrahalo light (IHL) and several emission lines. Accurate modeling of all three is essential to forecast detectability and interpret measurements. We present simulated SPHEREx intensity maps of all three on a lightcone, painted on halos from the Hidden Valley $N$-body simulation, and the CMB-lensing convergence of the same lightcone, over $100\,{\rm deg}^2$ to $z \approx 6$. We assign each halo its lines and continuum by stellar-population synthesis, in two models whose metallicities are fixed or follow its stellar mass. Halo-model predictions from the simulation's luminosity-halo mass relations and measured clustering, without free parameters, match the auto-spectra of the IGL and lines, and their cross-spectra with lensing, across the band: at $2.2\,μ$m, to within $5\%$ above $\ell \approx 400$ and $7\%$ above $\ell = 200$, respectively. The agreement requires nonlinear clustering: linear theory describes the cross-spectrum of a line up to $\ell \approx 1000$-$1600$ at $2.2\,μ$m, but fails for the IGL and the convergence at multipoles of a few hundred. With the noise of a SPHEREx deep field and of Simons Observatory lensing, the unfiltered cross-spectra, each component taken alone, reach signal-to-noise ratios of $9$-$21$ for the lines, $20$ for the IGL and $15$ for the IHL. A filter that removes radial modes longer than about $600$ Mpc keeps $62\%$ of the IGL's signal-to-noise and at most $20\%$ of the lines', with fitted amplitudes within about $1σ$ of the predictions before and after filtering. The emission model changes a channel's intensity by up to a factor of three, but the line detectability only by tens of percent.

papers.t: Cross-correlating the SPHEREx extragalactic background light with CMB lensing I: theoretical predictions and forecasts
papers.abs: The near-infrared extragalactic background light (EBL), which SPHEREx maps in 102 spectral channels, holds the emission lines of galaxies on top of a much brighter continuum from the integrated galaxy light (IGL) and the intrahalo light (IHL). Cross-correlating these maps with the lensing of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) isolates the emission that traces the matter, unbiased by uncorrelated foregrounds. The lines face two obstacles. Filtering along the line of sight removes the long radial modes that carry the cross-correlation, and the extragalactic continuum, a signal in its own right, is a correlated foreground for the lines. We forecast the detectability of all EBL components, in a common halo-model framework, for the SPHEREx deep fields and all-sky survey with lensing maps at the sensitivity level of Planck and the Simons Observatory (SO). Without filtering, and with all amplitudes fitted jointly, the cross-correlation with Planck lensing detects the IGL at $9σ$ in the deep fields, but not the lines. In the all-sky survey, it measures the IGL and IHL amplitudes to $1.0\%$ and $3\%$ and detects the five lines, fitted as one template, at $4.6σ$. With SO lensing, these become $0.6\%$, $1.6\%$ and $7.4σ$. In these joint fits, a filter removing radial modes longer than about $600$ Mpc costs every component $90\%$ or more of its signal-to-noise ratio, so the lines are reached by fitting the continuum, not by filtering it. These values assume a known spectral shape of the continuum. Calibrating it with the continuum's auto-spectra keeps the lines at $7.3$--$7.4σ$; fitting it from the cross-spectrum alone leaves $1.4$--$2.3σ$. The line detections vary by a factor of seven to eleven across line models. The cross-correlation is thus a robust probe of the IGL and a viable route to the emission lines, provided the continuum is modeled across the channels.

papers.t: A Science Traceability Matrix for Micro-arcsecond Resolution X-ray Imaging
papers.abs: Our ability to understand the highest energy processes and environments in astronomy is directly tied to our ability to probe their physical processes at the smallest scales. Despite transformative progress in high-angular resolution instruments across the radio through optical, angular resolution within the X-rays has plateaued around $\sim0.1-1''$, and therefore our window into the innermost regions of the high energy Universe lies primarily within spectral, timing, and/or polarimetric studies rather than direct imaging. This represents a significant barrier to gaining a robust understanding of key science questions, including the mechanisms of accretion and jet launching, the accretion activity and angular momentum losses of binary active galactic nuclei (AGN) leading to gravitational wave events, and the space weather events that may influence atmospheric evolution and prebiotic chemistry on potentially habitable exoplanets. The Accretion Explorer Interferometer (AEI) is a mission concept for X-ray imaging that could achieve up to $μ$as resolution, $\sim5-6$ orders of magnitude better than current instrumentation. Here we present the scientific discovery space enabled by such an advance, and highlight areas of uncertainty and open questions that are critical to investigate for future development of this concept.

papers.t: Diverse Stellar Components Resolved by JWST in the Massive Galaxy SPT0311-58
papers.abs: SPT0311$-$58 is comprised of two clumpy dusty star-forming galaxies inhabiting a $z=6.9$ protocluster core. Within a $16$ kpc diameter, there are 26 spectroscopically confirmed members. The 12 highly dust-obscured clumps were identified by their rest-frame [CII] emission, and the 14 less obscured clumps in the rest-frame ultraviolet (UV). We present new NIRCam and MIRI imaging from JWST of the central regions, which respectively trace the rest-frame UV and near-infrared. Combining this imaging with supplementary data from the Hubble Space Telescope and Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) provides the most complete picture of SPT0311$-$58 to date. Using 14 photometric bands and ALMA dust continuum to model the spectral energy distribution of SPT0311$-$58, we present well-informed stellar masses and star-formation rates (SFR) on local ($\sim1.5$ kpc) and global scales. We find that SPT0311$-$58 has a total stellar mass of $M_\star=3.2^{+3.2}_{-1.6}\times10^{11}\, M_\odot$ and SFR of $1.5^{+0.89}_{-0.53}\times10^3\, M_\odot\, \text{yr}^{-1}$. We compare these measurements to simulations and known, rare classes of high-redshift objects observed by JWST, namely massive $z\approx6$--$8.5$ Lyman-break galaxies, $z>6$ quasars, and other merging/clumpy $z\sim6$--$7$ systems. SPT0311$-$58 is comparable to $z>6$ quasars in both stellar mass and SFR, but is more extreme than the other reference populations for both quantities. Additionally, we compare our measurements with the star-formation histories (SFH) of five massive quiescent galaxies from the Early eXtragalactic Continuum and Emission Line Science (EXCELS) survey. We find that SPT0311$-$58 has a higher SFR than expected from the SFHs of the EXCELS galaxies at $z=6.9$, but is otherwise a plausible progenitor to massive quiescent galaxies.
papers.comment: 21 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables, Accepted to ApJ

papers.t: The phase gradient spectrum: probing the squeezed bispectrum of the 21-cm signal during reionization
papers.abs: The 21-cm signal from the epoch of reionization is highly non-Gaussian. Standard analyses rely on the power spectrum, which is blind to the Fourier phases, while higher-order statistics such as the bispectrum are computationally expensive and spread information across triangle configurations. As an efficient alternative, we develop the \textit{phase gradient spectrum}, which measures the circular coherence of phase differences between Fourier modes separated by a long-wavelength mode. We show analytically that this statistic measures the angle-averaged normalised squeezed bispectrum, which describes the response of small-scale power to long-wavelength fluctuations. Applied to reionization simulations with different ionizing source properties, the phase gradient spectrum of the 21-cm signal shows a characteristic non-monotonic evolution. At early times, the spectrum tracks the non-Gaussianity of the matter density field. Once the mean neutral fraction $\langle x_\mathrm{HI}\rangle \lesssim 0.9$, the spectrum follows the ionization topology. The phase coherence reaches a minimum midway through reionization and rises again as the remaining neutral regions shrink into isolated islands. Statistics that keep the sign of the squeezed bispectrum show that this minimum marks its sign change. This evolution holds for different reionization models and simulation frameworks. A Fisher forecast for a 1000-h Square Kilometre Array (SKA)-Low observation, combining five redshifts across reionization, shows that the phase gradient spectrum alone constrains the astrophysical parameters, and these constraints tighten by a factor of $\gtrsim 2$ for a 10,000-h observation. Combining the phase gradient spectrum with the power spectrum tightens the marginalised constraints by up to $\sim$20 per cent relative to the power spectrum alone.

papers.t: NEMESIS: Exoplanet TraNsit SurvEy of Nearby M-dwarfs in TESS FFIS II - 262 Transiting Planet Candidates from the TESS Primary Mission
papers.abs: We present NEMESIS II, a blind transit search of nearby M-dwarfs in TESS Primary Mission full-frame images (Sectors 1-26), including stars lacking 2-minute observations. Using the open-source NEMESIS pipeline, we extracted, detrended, and searched 213,658 single-sector light curves of 113,047 M-dwarfs within 100 pc, yielding 23,339 threshold crossing events. Automated LEO-Vetter vetting, applied identically to the survey and its injection-recovery and orbit-scrambling controls, retains 558 detections corresponding to 525 distinct signals with converged transit fits and periods of 0.51-9.10 days. Of these, 482 lie on stars without TOI, CTOI, or NASA Exoplanet Archive transiting-planet entries. Orbit-scrambling predicts 329 false alarms among the 558 detections, all but 14 of them among the 408 below Multiple Event Statistic 8. Assuming an astrophysical signal, TRICERATOPS favors a planetary origin for 262 of 525 candidates (232 new), which we classify as planet candidates; it also excludes resolved-neighbor eclipses for 105. Known planets and TOI candidates survive vetting at 1.01 +/- 0.07 of the injection-predicted rate. Correcting for each light curve's sensitivity, false alarms, and astrophysical false positives, we infer 0.81 +/- 0.44 planets per star for periods between 1.0-10.0 days and planet radii between 0.5-11.0 Earth radii. This is a lower limit, because our injections recover few or no planets near and below 1 Earth radii and assume central transits. Light curves, catalogs, vetting reports, and injection-recovery results will be released as a High Level Science Product at MAST upon publication. Documentation for the NEMESIS pipeline is available at https://nemesis-tess.readthedocs.io/.

papers.t: The Impact of Seeding Threshold on Wandering Black Hole Populations and Merger Rates
papers.abs: Cosmological simulations following massive black holes (MBHs) with dynamical friction subgrid models predict hundreds to thousands of off-centre, wandering MBHs in massive galaxies. We investigate how the wandering MBH population changes with halo mass seeding threshold. We present cosmological zoom-in simulations of a $(15\,\mathrm{cMpc})^3$ volume to $z=2$, using the halo mass seeding thresholds of ASTRID, EAGLE and Illustris-TNG $(5\times10^{9}-5\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}/h)$, with a fixed MBH seed mass of $m_\mathrm{seed}=2\times10^{6}\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}/h$. The subgrid dynamical friction model for MBHs switches to accurate integration around MBHs using the \textsc{ketju} module above $m_{\bullet} \geq 2\times10^{7}\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}/h$. We find that the seeding threshold greatly affects the MBH population: the number of seeded MBHs varies by a factor of ten and the number of wandering MBHs in the most massive galaxy ($M_\star=4.4\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) varies from 2 to 115. An MBH can become a wanderer in two ways. Interactions with other galaxies can offset a central MBH in low-mass galaxies ($M_\star\sim10^{8}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) if seeded in low mass halos $(\lesssim10^{10}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot/h)$. Alternatively, wandering MBHs can be added through mergers. The growth of the most massive MBHs is insensitive to the seeding threshold. While the total number of MBH mergers varies by an order of magnitude, the number of massive dynamically resolved MBH mergers differs by most a factor of $\sim3$ between seeding thresholds. The dynamically resolved binaries coalesce typically on timescales of $\sim10-250\,\mathrm{Myr}$ after becoming bound.
papers.comment: 19 pages, 13 figures, Metadata update only: author name corrected; no changes to content

papers.t: XQR30: ALMA Observations Reveal the Diverse Structure of Cold Gas within z>6 Quasar Host Galaxies
papers.abs: We present 0.25(~1.5kpc) ALMA observations of the [CII] and dust continuum emission from the host galaxies of 24 luminous z~6 quasars. Together with archival data from 17 quasars, this constitutes a nearly complete sample of all quasars with J-band magnitudes of J_AB<20.0 and redshifts between 5.8 and 6.6, which are the limits defined in the VLT/XSHOOTER legacy survey, XQR-30. For the full sample of 41 quasars, we find that 39(95%) of the quasar host galaxies are detected in [CII] emission with [CII] luminosities ranging between (0.3 and 9.2)x10^9Lsun, and 39(95%) of the quasar host galaxies are detected in continuum emission with continuum flux densities ranging between 0.22 and 16.3mJy. We detect eight [CII]-emitting companion galaxies, which is consistent with the expected number of galaxies based on clustering results. We find that z~6 quasar host galaxies have a range of morphologies, and by defining a new parameter, the kinematic position angle alignment parameter, Delta_PA_{kin-CII}, we show that most quasar host galaxies deviate from a standard disk model. This suggests that [CII] emission probes structures beyond simple disk rotation, such as bars, tidally disturbed gas, etc. We show that the dust emission is more compact than the [CII] emission independent of the morphology of the galaxy. Finally, we provide rough dynamical mass estimates within twice the [CII] half-light radius for the majority of the galaxies, and show that the average dynamical mass within the inner few kpc is consistent with estimates of the average mass in stars, gas and the SMBH.

papers.t: Mapping the multimessenger horizon for γ-ray counterparts of cosmic neutrinos
papers.abs: The joint detection of high-energy neutrinos and $γ$-rays offers a powerful probe of the most energetic astrophysical accelerators, linking hadronic interactions to observable signatures across cosmic distances. Understanding the conditions under which these two messengers can be simultaneously observed is essential for identifying and characterizing the sources of cosmic neutrinos. In this work, we examine the detectability of $γ$-ray cascades associated with neutrino production in source environments that are gamma-ray transparent, focusing on how electromagnetic cascades evolve as $γ$-rays propagate through intergalactic space. By modeling photon interactions with the extragalactic background light and deflections in intergalactic magnetic fields, we determine the minimum neutrino fluence for transient emission and neutrino flux for steady emission required to produce a $γ$-ray counterpart detectable by $γ$-ray observatories, such as Fermi-LAT, HAWC, or LHAASO. This defines a ``multimessenger horizon" -- the region in flux-distance parameter space where neutrinos and $γ$-rays are jointly observable. We consider both energy-binned injection tied to IceCube's sensitivity and a continuous power-law spectrum extending from TeV to PeV energies. Our results reveal that detectability depends strongly on redshift, magnetic field strength, and photon energy, with higher-energy cascades suffering greater attenuation inside filamentary structures. The framework provides new constraints on source opacity, baryon loading, and neutrino production mechanisms, offering a predictive tool for interpreting current events and guiding future multimessenger campaigns.

papers.t: From active nests to fast wind gusts: Nested flux emergence as a precursor of persistent non-axisymmetric coronal holes
papers.abs: Recurring flux emergence within active nests reshapes the Sun's large-scale magnetic field and creates unipolar magnetic regions that can support coronal holes. The fast solar wind emerging from coronal holes drives space weather across the heliosphere. We investigated how the emergence of active nests at the peak of solar cycle 25 drove changes in global magnetic topology, coronal hole formation, and solar wind speed. Coronal holes were identified from composite SDO/AIA maps and their magnetic field properties were extracted from SDO/HMI magnetograms. Spherical harmonic decomposition quantified how magnetic flux was distributed at different spatial scales and was used to extrapolate the coronal field. We compared coronal structure with SOHO/LASCO-C2 observations and the solar wind measured at 1 au. Emerging magnetic flux within active nests rapidly surpassed the pre-existing magnetic flux in 2024, strengthening the non-axisymmetric field and shifting the corona into a tilted-dipole state. This dipolarisation stabilised the large-scale magnetic field, with the heliospheric current sheet anchored above active nests. Unipolar magnetic regions from the edges of active nests sustained non-axisymmetric coronal holes covering 6 to 14% of the solar surface in 2025, comparable to the 12% covered by polar coronal holes at solar minimum. Flux emergence near the tilted-dipole's negative pole returned the corona to a quadrupole-dominated state in 2026. Active nests helped stabilise the coronal magnetic field, while the decay and transport of unipolar magnetic flux sustained persistent, non-axisymmetric coronal holes. Differential rotation between unipolar regions triggered episodic expansion and contraction of the largest coronal holes. Early identification of specific active nest configurations, combined with the solar cycle phase, could improve the forecasting of coronal holes and fast solar wind.
papers.comment: Accepted to A&A. 11 Pages + Appendix. 7 Figures + 4 Appendix Figures

papers.t: Flash UV Spectroscopy: Decoding the Ultraviolet Diversity of Young Core-Collapse Supernovae with the Hubble Space Telescope
papers.abs: We present multi-wavelength observations and modeling of the largest sample to date of core-collapse supernovae (SNe) with Hubble Space Telescope (HST) ultraviolet (UV) spectroscopy within < 2 weeks of first light. Our total sample contains early-time UV spectroscopy from 12 Type II SNe (SNe II), 3 Type IIb SNe (SNe IIb), 3 Type IIn SNe (SNe IIn) and 1 Type I super-luminous SN (SLSN-I). This sample includes 11 objects with unpublished UV spectroscopy from HST Cycles 31 and 32 "Flexible Thursdays" target of opportunity programs, increasing the number of core-collapse SNe with early-time HST UV spectra by a factor of 2.4. The early-time near-UV spectra of most sample SNe II show similar Doppler-broadened P-Cygni profiles of metals (Mg, Fe, Ti, Cr), though with notable diversity in line velocities and absorption strengths. Comparison to non-Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (nLTE) radiative transfer model grids at similar phases indicates that most sample SNe II are consistent with low circumstellar material (CSM) densities at the time of UV observations (e.g., $\dot M = 10^{-6}$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$, $v_w = 50$ km/s) and standard kinetic energies (e.g., $E_k = 0.6-1.2$ B), while two objects, SNe 2024faq and 2023ixf, show UV/optical evidence for interaction with more confined, higher-density CSM. SN 2023ixf and sample SNe IIn exhibit relatively featureless early-time UV spectra despite displaying prominent optical Lorentzian emission lines from electron scattering in optically thick CSM -- this being attributed to differing properties of UV resonance versus optical recombination transitions as well as intrinsic CSM asymmetries. These results demonstrate the potential of early-time UV spectroscopy to constrain the outermost SN ejecta structure, explosion energetics/composition, and progenitor mass-loss histories of core-collapse SNe.

papers.t: Active Galactic Nuclei as Beyond the Standard Model Laboratories: a White Paper
papers.abs: Multi-messenger and multi-wavelength observations of Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) can provide otherwise inaccessible knowledge about physics Beyond the Standard Model (BSM), and may even lead to its discovery. Realizing this potential hinges on two parallel efforts: advancing our understanding of AGN and of the dark matter around them, and identifying the BSM signatures that are at once promising and robust against the gaps in that understanding. These fields have attracted growing interest in recent years, also motivated by the IceCube association of neutrinos to individual AGN, yet we have only begun to explore their cross-fertilization. This white paper offers a new perspective on this interdisciplinary endeavor. It concisely reviews the state of the art in each field and at their interface, and identifies the key open questions that must be addressed to strengthen our prospects for learning about BSM physics with AGN.

papers.t: Shocks and Trails in the Circumgalactic Medium Driven by Runaway Supermassive Black Holes
papers.abs: Runaway supermassive black holes (SMBHs) have long been predicted. RBH-1, discovered with HST and confirmed by JWST, provides the strongest evidence yet for a runaway SMBH: a bow shock and linear trail in the circumgalactic medium (CGM) of a $z=0.96$ galaxy. The bow shock is $\sim$kpc wide, the trail is $\sim 60$ kpc long, and the SMBH apparently moves at $\sim 1,000$ km s$^{-1}$. Using controlled hydrodynamic simulations, we show that the SMBH's gravity alone cannot produce a significant bow shock, but a comoving wind source can sustain one similar to RBH-1's. The wind must either be active or have shut off less than $\sim 3$ Myr ago. The required recent wind momentum flux is $6\times10^{32}\,{\rm dyn}\,(n_{\rm CGM}/10^{-3}\,{\rm cm}^{-3})$, where $n_{\rm CGM}$ is the CGM density. Assuming the wind reaches peak strength only during the last $\sim 6$ Myr, the minimum integrated wind mass is $3.5\times10^5\,M_\odot\,(n_{\rm CGM}/10^{-3}\,{\rm cm}^{-3})$. A $2\times10^7\,M_\odot$ SMBH accreting at $1\%$ Eddington could power the wind. Supernova feedback from a star cluster carried by the SMBH is an alternative, although the required mass and momentum fluxes $\gtrsim 60$ Myr after ejection are difficult to reconcile with a standard initial mass function. For a hot ambient CGM at $\sim 10^6$ K, the quasi-linear trail constrains the 1D velocity dispersion to $σ_{\rm 1D}\lesssim 30$ km s$^{-1}$, above which it becomes strongly disturbed. Runaway SMBH trails therefore offer a new probe of turbulence in the diffuse CGM, in regimes where its kinematics are otherwise inaccessible.

papers.t: The meaning of Milky Way mass estimates in the presence of the LMC
papers.abs: The LMC's recent arrival perturbs the observed kinematics of the Milky Way's (MW) stellar halo, complicating equilibrium-based MW mass estimates at Galactocentric distances $r\gtrsim 30$ kpc. Using N-body MW+LMC simulations, we show that the MW stellar halo can be used to disentangle the total MW+LMC, current LMC, and pre-infall MW mass profiles, by exploiting the LMC's orbital path and the LMC-induced motion of the MW's center of mass ("reflex motion"). Tracers in regions crossed by the LMC longest ago (Galactic coordinates $\ell >0^\circ, b>0^\circ$) are approximately relaxed and trace the total MW+LMC mass. Since the reflex motion is primarily latitudinal, a radial-velocity-only estimator ($M_{v_r}$) recovers the total MW+LMC mass with $\lesssim 5\%$ errors across $30 0^\circ$) from those in its recent-orbit region ($\ell > 0^\circ, b 0^\circ, b>0^\circ$ and $50<r/{\rm kpc}<60$, we obtain a total MW+LMC mass $M(r<60\,{\rm kpc}) \approx 7.5^{+3.0}_{-2.2}\times 10^{11}\,M_\odot$. Observationally, recovering the LMC and pre-infall MW mass profiles requires 6D samples at $r\gtrsim100$ kpc, and a virial mass to within $\sim10-20\%$ requires $r\gtrsim120$ kpc, both achievable with Gaia DR5 astrometry for halo giants targeted by DESI Run 2 and 4MOST. Rather than treating the LMC-induced disequilibrium as an obstacle, our framework exploits it to weigh both galaxies.
papers.comment: Submitted to ApJ, 26 pages (main text), 22 figures - comments welcome

papers.t: Baryonification V: Thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich maps from dark-matter-only lightcones
papers.abs: Baryonic feedback is a major theoretical uncertainty for Stage-IV weak lensing (WL) surveys. The thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ) effect traces the hot gas redistributed by feedback, so combining it with WL can calibrate feedback and improve cosmological constraints. Doing so with simulation-based inference requires correlated lensing and Compton-$y$ maps across many cosmologies and feedback scenarios. We present two methods to generate Compton-$y$ maps from dark-matter-only $N$-body light cones using the component-wise baryonification (BFC) model, which produces separate gas and stellar fields and computes the gas pressure from hydrostatic equilibrium. The two methods, painting pressure profiles onto halos or redistributing the signal along the baryonified gas, agree to within a few per cent. We calibrate the model to the fiducial and strongest AGN feedback FLAMINGO simulations by jointly fitting gas mass fractions and thermal pressure profiles, measuring the non-thermal pressure from the simulated gas velocities rather than treating it as a free parameter. The predicted Compton-$y$ profiles match FLAMINGO within halo-to-halo scatter, and when painted onto the FLAMINGO halos we reproduce the tSZ power spectrum of both feedback models to $\sim5\%$ for $500\lesssim\ell\lesssim3000$. Applied to a \emph{CosmoGridV1-like} $N$-body simulation, our maps agree with FLAMINGO within $\sim10\%$ for $300\lesssim\ell\lesssim8000$; the remaining differences come from the few hundred most massive clusters, and removing them from both halo catalogs brings the two into agreement. Our method thus enables accurate and efficient tSZ forward models from $N$-body simulation suites such as CosmoGridV1, an important step towards joint WL and tSZ simulation-based inference for Euclid, LSST, and the Simons Observatory.
papers.comment: 39 pages, 18 figures, 3 tables, to be submitted to JCAP

papers.t: ASAS-SN Rates V: Tidal Disruption Event Volumetric Rates and Luminosity Functions by Optical Spectroscopic Type, X-ray Luminosity, and Host-Galaxy Properties
papers.abs: We present volumetric rates and luminosity functions (LFs) of tidal disruption events (TDEs) based on 21 TDEs from the All-Sky Automated Survey for Supernovae (ASAS-SN) between 2014 and 2024. We calculate completeness corrections from injection-recovery simulations of the ASAS-SN light curves using individual TDE templates. We find a total volumetric rate of $\log_{10}(R_{\rm tot}[{\rm yr}^{-1}{\rm Gpc}^{-3}h_{70}^3]) = 2.32^{+0.15}_{-0.23}$ for $z \leq 0.12$. We also measure the rates of two growing TDE subpopulations. The one off-nuclear TDE in our standard sample implies $\log_{10}(R_{\rm off\text{-}nuclear}) = 0.39^{+0.52}_{-0.76}$ ($1.2^{+3.4}_{-1.0}$% of the total rate). We measure the rate of recurrent TDEs (rTDEs) to be $\log_{10}(R_{\rm recurrent}) = 1.26^{+0.23}_{-0.62}$ ($9^{+8}_{-6}$% of the total rate) from the four rTDEs in our standard sample, increasing to $1.45^{+0.20}_{-0.35}$ ($13^{+10}_{-7}$%) when the well-studied ASASSN-14ko is included. Galaxies with substantial (>0.1%) burst-mass fractions and steeply falling star-formation histories host the majority of TDEs. We recover the known overrepresentation of TDEs in post-starburst galaxies, by a factor of $15^{+16}_{-11}$ relative to matched control galaxies, and a weaker enhancement of $5^{+5}_{-4}$ in quiescent Balmer-strong galaxies. TDE-H+He events dominate the volumetric TDE rate, with TDE-H, TDE-He, and TDE-Featureless events comprising <15% of nearby TDEs. The $g$-band LFs are statistically indistinguishable when split at the median X-ray to UV/optical blackbody luminosity ratio of $\sim$1%, corroborating unification models where the observed multi-wavelength emission is set primarily by viewing angle effects. Extrapolating the measured TDE LFs to higher luminosities and more massive black holes supports a TDE origin for luminous ambiguous nuclear transients and extreme nuclear transients.
papers.comment: 23 pages, 10 figures, 8 tables. Submitted to The Open Journal of Astrophysics

papers.t: Supernova Bounds on Neutrino Dipole Moments from a Modern Perspective
papers.abs: Neutrinos may have nonstandard magnetic dipole moments $μ_ν$. In the dense cores of supernovae (SNe), these would convert part of the neutrinos into sterile, right-handed states through the electromagnetic fluctuations of the charged plasma. The streaming sterile neutrinos with 100-MeV energies can convert back to standard neutrinos in the Galactic magnetic field, leading to a high-energy neutrino flux unobserved from the historical SN 1987A.
